title: Lester's sensitivity and the rumors about his manner
summary: Asked about rumors of effeminacy, Jones insists Lester was tender and hated seeing anyone mistreated.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I think right now since we're talking about him and you were his coworker and everything, because of Lester's very light complexion, because he was a fair-skinned black man -
But it wasn't his problem. But because he was fair-skinned and because he was very delicate and because he called people Lady, there was a great amongst people outside of the music business -
They thought it was an effeminate thing. No, course not.
Would you straighten that out for the record?
Because I know there was nothing bisexual -

Because if you really think he's homosexual, HINTON: Queer. go in the room with him, you'll find out what he is. Oh, HINTON: I'm glad to hear you say that. no. J. He was too tender, he was too tender. He just didn't like to see nobody, not one human being, mistreat another human being. Lester Young could be playing his horn and when a person came in that wasn't [ tape breaks off here ], he would sense this like a dog or cat. He would not play his horn right and he never told you or me why he didn't like the person. He let you find out for yourself. He'd always say, "Um, I Feel a draft." They didn't know what he meant. He would excuse himself and he always said, "How's your feelings?" and he would leave. He would quickly leave. But when he found out, Milt, that you did something wrong to me, he did not like that. You didn't do nothing to Lester, but he didn't like for you to mistreat a human being. He just didn't understand why the people in the world was - why you mistreat people. He didn't understand it.
He was very sensitive. He was better than radar. He could just feel - he said, "Mm, I'm getting silence, J. He says J., I'm trying to tell them - what can I do?"
I said, "Nothing, Pres. We just keep on playing." He says, "What can I do?"
